open_points.subject: ownership and interface for command-line argument-count validation
open_points.text: `surface.serve_kernel` takes “The configuration file path” but says “a command line without exactly one argument stops the start like a failing check of public_op:installation.load_installation”; State 4 instead says `capability:installation.load_installation` checks that “the command line holds exactly one argument”, while `installation.load_installation` accepts only one already-selected path and cannot observe the command-line count.
open_points.question: Which operation receives the raw command-line arguments and owns the exactly-one-argument check, and what does the other operation receive after that check?
options: `surface.serve_kernel` receives the argument vector, checks its cardinality, and passes the sole path to `installation.load_installation`.
`installation.load_installation` receives the argument vector and performs both the cardinality and absolute-path checks.
The host entry point checks cardinality before calling `surface.serve_kernel`, which receives only the sole path.
open_points.default_guess: `surface.serve_kernel` receives the argument vector, checks that it contains exactly one configuration-path argument, and passes that path to `installation.load_installation`, which checks that it is absolute.
